The main takeaway from our work is that

the partition function and information rate of two dimensional models can be estimated by Monte Carlo methods that are based on sampling a cycle breaking subset, which is much smaller than the total number of variables in the model.
, for a large class of graphical models, it is possible to estimate the partition function and/or the information rate with a complexity that grows only logarithmically with the system size.
the cycle breaking subset of variables can be determined by a greedy algorithm, and the exact sum-product computations can be performed efficiently.
